title: Relative smooth SNC resolution of a tame semilinear quotient
statement: Let $F$ be a field and $K/F$ a finite separable field extension [def-weil-field] [def-pc-field-extension]. Let $H$ be a finite group of order invertible in $F$, acting on $K$ by $F$-automorphisms. Let $Y$ be a smooth projective $K$-scheme [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] [def-kun-projective] with an action of $H$ by $F$-scheme automorphisms, equivariantly for $Y\to\operatorname{Spec}K$. Let $D\subseteq Y$ be an invariant reduced relative strict normal crossings divisor over $K$ [def-trf-smooth-strict-normal-crossings-divisor]: it is effective Cartier, has finitely many distinct integral components, and the intersection of any $r$ distinct components is empty or smooth over $K$ of pure codimension $r$. Suppose $q:Y\to Q=Y/H$ is the finite categorical geometric scheme quotient, with orbit geometric fibres and invariant structure sheaf [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism]. There are a smooth projective $F$-scheme $R$ and a projective surjective morphism $v:R\to Q$ [def-trf-projective-bundle-morphism] [def-weil-surjective-morphism] which is an isomorphism on a dense open meeting every component of $Q$, and induces a bijection of irreducible-component generic points and equality of their residue fields [def-weil-irreducible-components] [def-sc-generic-point] [def-weil-residue-field]. The reduced closed subscheme with support $v^{-1}(q(|D|))$ is a relative strict normal crossings divisor on $R/F$. Its irreducible components are smooth over $F$, and every intersection of $r$ distinct components is empty or smooth over $F$ of pure codimension $r$. Locally on $R$ the components through a point have equations which are distinct members of a regular system of parameters [def-weil-pbc-regular-system-of-parameters]; thus the same reduced divisor is a strict normal crossings boundary on the regular scheme $R$ [def-trf-strict-normal-crossings-boundary] [def-weil-regular-scheme]. Disconnected $Y$, a nonfaithful action on $Y$ or $K$, and the empty divisor are allowed. Projective over a field means admitting a closed immersion into a finite-dimensional projective space over that field. Field-extension terminology and degrees are as in [def-pc-field-tower].

source.place: Expose X Theorem 1.1, printed pp.135--136, and 2.3 Step 3, pp.151--152: component stabilizers modulo generic inertia, orbit induction, projective log modification of the quotient and saturated monoidal resolution (VIII 3.4.9); the trivial-base log chart from X 1.2 gives relative smoothness. Strictification and parameter/intersection criterion: VIII 4.1.2--4.1.8 and 4.2.2(i), pp.117--118. Boundary is the inverse image of the image of the original divisor, not the whole auxiliary enlarged boundary.

proof.text: The finite separable map $\operatorname{Spec}K\to\operatorname{Spec}F$ is etale by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-separable-extension-etale], hence smooth of relative dimension zero by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-smooth-zero-dimensional-fibres]. Smooth composition [lem-trf-smooth-composition] shows that $Y$ and every intersection of components of $D$ are smooth over $F$. Their codimensions are unchanged, since their schemes have not changed. Thus $D$ is also relative SNC over $F$. The supplied semilinear quotient geometry [lem-sfb-semilinear-quotient-projective-geometry], with $e=F$, gives that $Y,Q$ are normal Noetherian, $Y$ is a finite disjoint union of clopen integral components, and $Y/F$ is projective. The same statement gives $Q$ the unique $F$-structure for which $q$ is an $F$-morphism, and shows $Q$ proper of finite type, in particular separated, over $F$; nothing more about $Q$ is used below.

source.place: X 2.3 Step 3, p.151, separable constants and smooth pairs; projectivity of supplied semilinear quotient as in Step 2.

proof.text: Partition the finitely many components of $Y$ into $H$-orbits. Each orbit union $Y_a$ is clopen and invariant, and its image $Q_a$ is clopen: both it and its complement are images of closed subsets under the finite map. The restricted quotient has all the required properties by [lem-sfb-clopen-geometric-categorical-quotient]. Choose a component $C_a$ and let $G_a$ be its stabilizer. On an affine open of $Q_a$, sections upstairs form a product indexed by these components. An invariant tuple is determined uniquely by its component on $C_a$, which must be $G_a$-invariant; the other entries are its translates. The orbit-fibre assertion restricts in the same way, and an invariant map from $C_a$ extends to $Y_a$ by translates. Consequently $C_a\to Q_a$ is the finite categorical geometric quotient by $G_a$. It is surjective, and $Q_a$ is integral because it is reduced and the image of the irreducible $C_a$.

source.place: X 2.3 Step 3, pp.151--152, component stabilizers and induction over each orbit.

proof.text: Let $I_a$ be the kernel of $G_a\to\operatorname{Aut}_F(\kappa(C_a))$. An element of this kernel is the identity on $C_a$: apply [lem-sfb-relative-separated-dominant-ext] to the two maps from the reduced scheme $C_a$ to the separated $F$-scheme $C_a$, and to $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(C_a)\to C_a$. Thus $I_a$ is normal and acts trivially on the scheme and its boundary. The action factors through $\overline G_a=G_a/I_a$ and the quotient stays $Q_a$. For each nonidentity element the equalizer with the identity is closed, since the diagonal of $C_a/F$ is closed [def-weil-proper-morphism], and misses the generic point by the definition of $I_a$. Remove the finite union of these proper fixed loci. The complement is invariant, dense, and free on geometric points. The order of $\overline G_a$ is invertible in $F$, because it divides $|H|$. This is the generically free effective action required by Gabber.

source.place: X 2.3 Step 3, p.151, stabilizer modulo inertia at the generic point.

proof.text: Restriction to the clopen component $C_a$ preserves smoothness [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-restrict-open-subschemes]. The restrictions of the integral components of $D$ are either empty or unchanged, so $D_a=D\cap C_a$ is relative SNC. By the converse clause of [lem-sfb-free-characteristic-relative-nc-criterion], condition (a) holds: its divisorial log structure is fs, log smooth over the trivial log field $F$, and has triviality locus exactly $C_a\setminus D_a$; that criterion also makes $(C_a,D_a)$ log regular. The action of $\overline G_a$ preserves this structure. Apply [lem-sfb-field-log-smooth-gabber-modification] to obtain $h_a:W_a\to C_a$ and $P_a=W_a/\overline G_a$ with log-smooth log-regular quotient boundary $B_a$. In particular the image in $P_a$ of $h_a^{-1}D_a$ is contained in $B_a$. Since $C_a/F$ is projective and $h_a$ is projective in the finite-space convention, [lem-trf-h-projective-composition] makes $W_a/F$ projective. The new node gives $P_a$ integral with a locally closed immersion $j:P_a\to\mathbf P^n_F$, so $P_a/F$ is separated of finite type. By [lem-sfb-finite-constant-projective-graph] over $S=\operatorname{Spec}F$, $W_a$ and $\mathbf P^n_F$ are proper over $F$; as $p_a:W_a\to P_a$ is surjective, [lem-weil-pbc-image-universally-closed] makes $P_a/F$ proper, and [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-theoretic-image-proper] for $j$ over $\operatorname{Spec}F$ shows $j(P_a)$ closed in $\mathbf P^n_F$. Writing $j$ as a closed immersion into an open $U$, the ideal of $j(P_a)$ on $U$ and the unit ideal on $\mathbf P^n_F\setminus j(P_a)$ glue, so $j$ is a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion] and $P_a/F$ is projective [def-kun-projective]. The categorical property gives $f_a:P_a\to Q_a$ with $f_ap_a=c_ah_a$; it is an $F$-morphism, because both maps $P_a\to\operatorname{Spec}F$ factor the same invariant map from $W_a$ through $p_a$.

source.place: X Theorem 1.1, pp.135--136; X 2.3 Step 3, diagram (2.d), p.151.

proof.text: Put $U_a=P_a\setminus B_a$. By [lem-sfb-field-log-smooth-gabber-modification], $P_a$ is integral of finite type over $F$ and its fs divisorial log structure is log regular and log smooth over the trivial log field, with triviality locus exactly $U_a$. Thus all hypotheses of [lem-sfb-equivariant-log-smooth-fan-regularization] hold with trivial group. It gives a projective birational tower $A_a\to P_a$, with $A_a$ smooth over $F$ and reduced inverse-image boundary having smooth coordinate normal-crossings charts. Apply [lem-sfb-relative-nc-maximal-branch-strictification], again with trivial group, to get a projective birational morphism $R_a\to A_a$ with $R_a$ smooth and integral and full reduced boundary $\widetilde E_a$ relative strict normal crossings. Both citations allow imperfect $F$ and empty boundary. Each tower is projective in the projective-bundle sense. Their composite with the projective $P_a/F$ is projective by [lem-sfb-projective-bundle-composition]. The structure sheaf on the affine scheme $\operatorname{Spec}F$ is ample directly from [def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module], so [lem-trf-projective-bundle-to-h-projective] makes $R_a/F$ projective in the finite-space convention.

The modification $h_a$ identifies the function fields of $W_a,C_a$ equivariantly. By [lem-sfb-finite-quotient-generic-fields] for the normal Noetherian $C_a\to Q_a$, $\kappa(Q_a)=\kappa(C_a)^{G_a}=\kappa(C_a)^{\overline G_a}$ with its actual embedding. For $p_a$, take an affine open $V\subseteq P_a$; $p_a^{-1}V=\operatorname{Spec}A$ is affine as $p_a$ is finite, $A$ is a domain and $\mathcal O(V)=A^{\overline G_a}$. An invariant fraction $a/b$ equals $a\prod_{g\ne1}g(b)/\prod_g g(b)$ with invariant denominator, hence invariant numerator, so $\kappa(P_a)=\kappa(W_a)^{\overline G_a}=\kappa(C_a)^{\overline G_a}$. As $f_ap_a=c_ah_a$ is surjective, $f_a$ maps generic point to generic point and induces the identity of $\kappa(C_a)^{\overline G_a}$ on these embeddings. Both later towers are birational, so $v_a:R_a\to Q_a$ also induces this same function-field isomorphism. By [lem-sfb-finite-constant-projective-graph] with $k=F$ and constant extension $F/F$, $v_a$ is projective and proper. Its image is closed by the definition of properness [def-weil-proper-morphism] and contains the generic point, so it is surjective. Properness includes separatedness and finite type. On affine charts over the Noetherian target, [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-noetherian-finite-presentation] gives finite presentation of the ring maps; hence the map is locally of finite presentation by [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. Applying [lem-sfb-birational-isomorphism-dense-open] gives a dense open of $Q_a$ over which $v_a$ is an isomorphism. In particular it has exactly one component generic point, with unchanged residue field.

source.place: X 2.3 Step 3, pp.151--152, the quotient projective modifications v and w; Stacks 0BAJ for the dense-open conclusion.

proof.text: For the finite quotient $c_a:C_a\to Q_a$, the effective Cartier ideal of $D_a$ is invertible by [lemma-nagata-effective-cartier-is-invertible]. By [lem-sfb-finite-trivialize-invertible-upstairs], near any $z\in Q_a$ it has one generator $b$ on $c_a^{-1}V$. The product $N(b)=\prod_{g\in\overline G_a}g(b)$ is invariant and descends to $c\in\mathcal O_{Q_a}(V)$. Each factor is a nonzerodivisor generating the same ideal up to a unit, so the product is a nonzerodivisor; injectivity of the invariant-ring inclusion gives the same for $c$. Its vanishing support is exactly $c_a(D_a)\cap V$, because upstairs the zero set of the product is precisely $D_a$ and the quotient is surjective. This is the elementary conjugate-product argument after Stacks Tag 0BUT, not an application of a Cartier-image claim for arbitrary finite maps.

source.place: X 2.3 Step 3, p.152, retaining the original subboundary; Stacks divisors.tex Tag 0BUT (lemma-finite-trivialize-invertible-upstairs).

proof.text: The smooth scheme $R_a$ is regular by [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-scheme-over-field-regular]. Smoothness also makes every intersection of components of $\widetilde E_a$ regular; its pure codimension condition therefore gives the regular-intersection boundary of [def-trf-strict-normal-crossings-boundary]. By [lem-sfb-snc-boundary-parameter-criterion], its component equations at each point are distinct parameters $t_1,\ldots,t_r$. The inverse image of $c_a(D_a)$ is contained in $\widetilde E_a$ by construction. Pull back the equation $c$ of Step 7. It is nonzero, since $v_a$ is birational and $c$ is nonzero on integral $Q_a$, and is a unit off $\widetilde E_a$. By [lem-trf-regular-local-ufd-boundary-factorization] it is $u\prod t_i^{n_i}$. Thus its reduced zero set is precisely the union of the components with $n_i>0$. Globally the reduced inverse image $E_a=(v_a^{-1}c_a(D_a))_{\mathrm{red}}$ is a union of components of $\widetilde E_a$, hence is effective Cartier and relative SNC: every chosen intersection is one of the intersections for $\widetilde E_a$. The same parameter equations prove the required absolute boundary and local-parameter clauses. The unit equation gives the empty divisor.

source.place: X 2.3 Step 3, final paragraph p.152; VIII Remark 4.2.2(i), p.118; Stacks more-algebra.tex Tag 0AG0 (lemma-regular-local-UFD).

proof.text: Form $R=\coprod_a R_a$ and $v=\coprod_a v_a$ using [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-coproduct-family], with target $Q=\coprod_a Q_a$. The finite disjoint union is smooth by the source-local definition [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. To see projectivity explicitly, choose closed embeddings $R_a\hookrightarrow\mathbf P^{n_a}_F$ and place them in disjoint coordinate blocks of $\mathbf P^{\sum_a(n_a+1)-1}_F$. The block projective subspaces are pairwise disjoint closed subschemes, and their finite scheme-theoretic union is their coproduct (on each block's complement the other block ideals are units). This gives a closed embedding of $R$. The graph lemma [lem-sfb-finite-constant-projective-graph] now makes $v$ projective. Surjectivity, the dense isomorphism opens, the generic-point bijection and residue equalities hold on the clopen summands. The divisors $E_a$ glue on these disjoint summands; their support is exactly $v^{-1}(q(|D|))$, and their smooth intersections, parameter equations and boundary properties are local on those summands. If $Y$ is empty then $Q,R$ are empty, and all assertions hold with the empty divisor and empty open.
